misconceptions.title: Squared each term separately
misconceptions.what: You wrote $(a+b)^2$ as $a^2 + b^2$. Squaring a sum also makes a middle term, $2ab$.

misconceptions.title: Multiplied only the first term
misconceptions.what: The number outside the parentheses has to multiply every term inside, not just the first one.

misconceptions.title: Lost a sign when distributing a negative
misconceptions.what: A negative outside the parentheses changes the sign of every term inside.

misconceptions.title: Moved a term without changing its sign
misconceptions.what: Moving a term to the other side means doing the opposite operation to both sides, so its sign flips.

misconceptions.title: Divided only part of the equation
misconceptions.what: When you divide, every term on both sides has to be divided by the same number.

misconceptions.title: Subtracted the coefficient instead of dividing
misconceptions.what: $3x$ means $3 \times x$, so you undo it by dividing by 3, not subtracting 3.

misconceptions.title: Added fractions straight across
misconceptions.what: $\frac{1}{2} + \frac{1}{3}$ isn't $\frac{2}{5}$. Fractions need a common denominator before you add.

misconceptions.title: Combined unlike terms
misconceptions.what: $2x$ and $3$ aren't like terms, so they can't be added into $5x$.

misconceptions.title: Multiplied the variable when adding
misconceptions.what: $2x + 3x = 5x$. Adding like terms adds the numbers; the variable stays the same.

misconceptions.title: Mixed up the exponent rules
misconceptions.what: Multiplying powers adds exponents: $x^2 \cdot x^3 = x^5$. A power of a power multiplies them: $(x^2)^3 = x^6$.

misconceptions.title: Took the square root of each term
misconceptions.what: $\sqrt{x^2 + 9}$ is not $x + 3$. Square roots don't split across addition.

misconceptions.title: Halved instead of taking the square root
misconceptions.what: Undoing $x^2$ means taking the square root, not dividing by 2.

misconceptions.title: Forgot the negative square root
misconceptions.what: Both $7^2$ and $(-7)^2$ equal 49, so taking a square root gives two answers: $\pm$.

misconceptions.title: Divided by the variable and lost a solution
misconceptions.what: Dividing both sides by $x$ throws away $x = 0$. Move everything to one side and factor instead.

misconceptions.title: Lost a solution
misconceptions.what: This step dropped one of the equation's solutions.
